title: A Court Said Yes, but a Family Is Still Waiting
summary: For almost a year, one family has lived in two different countries while waiting for one important paper: a visa. Dustin Hoffman is a U.S. Army veteran. He started the paperwork late last year so his wife, Gloria, could live in the United States. Gloria is from Colombia. She stayed in Argentina with their 5-year-old daughter, Chaya, and Hoffman's 12-year-old stepson, Israel. Hoffman says he misses them every day. In January, the Trump administration stopped processing immigrant visas for people from 75 countries. Gloria is from Colombia, one of those countries. In August, a federal judge ordered the ban to be lifted. But the Hoffman family still has not got its visa. The State Department has asked for more proof that the family can support itself without public help. Lawyers for migrants say this shows a bigger problem. They say interviews and visa stamps are still moving slowly, so the court order has not ended the wait.
why_it_matters: Families should be able to live together, and rules about moving to a new country can change a child's everyday life.

background_read: A visa is a paper that lets a person move to and live in another country.
To get one, a family fills out forms and shows it can pay its own way, and then officials check the forms and hold interviews.
A court can order a rule to stop, but the family still has to wait until the checks are done.
